quotes.text:
* When all messages are successfully downloaded:
 *  - onDone() will be invoked with NS_OK.
 *
 * If an error occurs while downloading a message:
 *  - onDone() will be invoked with the failure code.
 *  - no more messages will be downloaded.
 *
 * If the call to ExchangeFetchMsgsToOffline() returns an error code,
 * no async operation will be started and onDone() will _not_
 * be invoked.
 *
 * If the call to ExchangeFetchMsgsToOffline() succeeds, it will return
 * NS_OK and the async operation will be started.
 * If the async operation is started, onDone() will _always_ be
 * invoked when it completes, with the resultant status.

source.basis: Quoted evidence supports the claim; its interpretation still needs current-source checks.

text: The accepted ExchangeFetchMsgsToOffline returns an immediate error without invoking onDone when the operation cannot start. A successful start promises a later onDone result. Its empty-list success is dispatched to the current thread instead of invoking inline. The channel failure callback sends OnStartRequest then OnStopRequest because AsyncOpen has already returned successfully. Scoped callback recommendation: keep these two error channels and the no-inline empty case explicit in documentation and tests. This is static source inspection. No runtime, build, lint or live accessibility check was run. Full Bugzilla and Phabricator discussion remains pending.
title: Exchange fetch completion distinguishes immediate failure from asynchronous completion
